full_judgment:
2. This is an application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure preferred before this Court at the instance of the accused-petitioner against order dated 28-4-2014 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka, in Special Case No. 17 of 2010, rejecting the application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 3. Facts relevant for disposal of this application are that on 13-6-2010 at about 6-55 PM one Nur Ahmed, Deputy Director of the Anti-Corruption Commission (hereinafter called 'ACC') as informant lodged First Information Report against the petitioner under section 26(2) (ka) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. 2004, (hereinafter called "the said Act") alleging, inter-alia, that the ACC issued a notice vide memo. No. দুদুক/বিঃঅনু ও তদন্ত ১-১৬-২০১০ dated 13-4- 2010 upon the petitioner under section 26(1) of the said Act, directing him to submit his wealth statement within 7(seven) working days from the date of receipt of the notice; but when the said notice was sent to the petitioner, he refused to receive the same. Subsequently, the notice was sent to him by registered post with AD. In the meantime, the petitioner filed a Civil Suit being Title Suit No. 250 of 2010 before the learned Joint District Judge. 1st Court, Dhaka, challenging the legality of the proceedings initiated by the ACC pursuant to the said notice and in the plaint of the said Suit, it is admitted that the notice was received by him on 19-4-2610. The petitioner also filed an application for temporary injunction praying for stay of the proceedings initiated pursuant to the said notice and the learned Joint District Judge after hearing the parties rejected the same. Challenging the same, the petitioner preferred appeal before this Hon'ble Court being FMA No. 218 of 2010 and after hearing the parities, their Lordships were pleased to issue a Rule and stayed operation of the said notice. Having aggrieved by the order, the ACC preferred Civil Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 331 of 2010 (later converted into Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 986 of 2010) and after hearing the parties, the Hon'ble Judge-in-Chamber of the Appellate Division stayed the operation of the said ad-interim order of the High Court Division vide order dated 5-5-2010. It was calculated by excluding period of stay granted by the High Court Division that 7(Seven) working days as directed by the ACC to submit wealth statement has already been expired and the petitioner has failed to submit his wealth statement prior to the expiry period of the seven working days, as such, he committed offence punishable under section 26(2) (Ka) of the said Act and the case was registered as Gulshan Police Station Case No. 38 dated 13-6-2010. 

 4. One Md Nur Mohammad, Deputy Director of the ACC as investigating officer, investigated the case and after holding investigation, submitted charge-sheet being No. 457 dated 15-7-2010 against the petitioner under section 26(2) (Ka) of the said Act. 

 5. The case was transmitted in the Court of learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka, for trial, wherein it was numbered as Metropolitan Special case No. 132 of 2010. Learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge took cognizance of the case under section 26(2) (Ka) of the said Act. The case was again transferred in the Court of Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka, for holding trial on 27-9-2009 and the same was registered as Special Case No. 17 of 2010. Thereafter, the accused-petitioner preferred an application under section 241-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for discharging from the allegation leveled against him. After hearing the parties, perusing the application and materials on record, the learned Special Judge rejected the application and framed charge against the accused-petitioner under section 26(2)(Ka) of the Anti-Corruption Act. 2004 vide order dated 28-4- 2014. 

 7. Learned Counsel Mr AJ Mohammad Ali appearing for the petitioner submits that the FIR, Charge-sheet and other materials on record shows that there are no ingredients of offence under section 26(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act 2004, as in nowhere it is stated or alleged that the accused- petitioner has acquired any property disproportionate to his legal source of income and, as such, framing of charge in the said section against the petitioner is illegal. He further submits that the petitioner preferred Title Suit No. 250 of 2010 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, on 12-4-2010 challenging legality of the proceedings of the Anti-Corruption Commission initiated against him, the accused-petitioner also moved an application for temporary injunction before the same Court on 21-4-2010 and prayed that the Anti-Corruption Commission be restrained by an order of injunction; however, the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, summarily rejected the application for temporary injunction on 21-4-2010. Challenging the said order, the petitioner preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal (FMA) No. 218 of 2010 before this Division alongwith an application for temporary injunction and after hearing the parties, their Lordships were pleased to admit the appeal, issued Rule and stayed operation of the said notice issued under section 26(1) of the said Act, vide order dated 27- 4-2010 passed in Civil Rule No. 235 (FM) of 2010; challenging the order, ACC preferred Provisional Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 331 of 2010 (later on converted to Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 986 of 2010) and after hearing the parties, the Hon'ble Judge-in-Chamber of the Appellate Division has been pleased to stay operation of the ad-interim order passed by the High Court Division vide order dated 5-5-2010; both the First Miscellaneous Appeal (FMA) No. 218 of 2010 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 986 of 2010 are pending for hearing before this Division and the Appellate Division respectively and both the cases deals with the legality of the notice dated 13-4-2010 issued under section 26(1) of the said Act; during pendency of these cases before this Hon'ble Court, the ACC has attempted to render the cases as infructuous by lodging FIR, submitting charge-sheet and arresting the accused petitioner; these actions of the ACC shows utter disrespect to the process of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh. He further submits that the accused-petitioner preferred an application under section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the High Court Division for quashing the proceedings of the instant case and a Division Bench of this Court after hearing the parties, perusing the application and materials on record, discharged the Rule and vacated the order of stay and directed the trial Court to conclude trial of the case expeditiously vide judgment and order dated 27- 5-2013; challenging the said order the accused petitioner preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 241 of 2013 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division; subsequently, the accused petitioner filed regular Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 369 of 2009 and the same is still pending for hearing before the Appellate Division of this Hon'ble Court. He next submits that even no order of stay is granted by the Appellate Division, the trial of the case will not proceed and the proceedings of the present case and framing charge during pendency of the subject matter of the case in the Appellate Division for adjudication is illegal, as such, framing charge under section 26(2)(Ka) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, against the accused-petitioner is unlawful and liable to be set-aside. The learned advocate for the accused-petitioner further submits section 26(1) of the said Act requires satisfaction of the ACC (after appropriate investigation) as to the unlawful acquisition of wealth; as such, the ACC is required to be objectively satisfied on the basis of investigation before issuance of a notice under section 26(1) of the said Act, but FIR and the investigation report dated 23-3-2010 prepared by the ACC does not disclose satisfaction of the Commission to the effect that the accused-petitioner has unlawfully acquired wealth; as such, the notice has been issued beyond scope of the said Act and framing of charge under section 26(2)(Ka) against the accused-petitioner is illegal and liable to be set-aside. He lastly submits that the ACC sent said notice to the accused-petitioner on 13-4-2010 under section 26(1) of the said Act directing him to submit his wealth statement within 7 (seven) working days upon receipt of the notice; the time of 7(seven) working days has already been expired and there is no efficacy of this notice and thus the ACC is required to issue a fresh notice. As such, instant proceeding under section 26(2) (Ka) of the said Act is not in conformity with the law and liable to be set-aside. 

 8. To substantiate his submission, learned advocate for the petitioner placed reliance in the cases of Moonsur Ahmed vs State, reported in 14 BLC 110, Mrs. Halima Khatun vs Bangladesh, reported in 30 DLR (AD 1978) 207, Kh. Ehtesham Uddin Ahmed @ Iqbal vs Bangladesh, reported in 33 DLR (AD 1981) 154, Sultan Ahmed vs Chief Election Commissioner, reported in 30 DLR (HC 1978)291. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned advocate appearing for the ACC submits that there is specific allegation against the accused-petitioner which attract the provisions of section 26(2) (Ka) of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act. He next submits that prior to the filing of the instant application, the accused-petitioner after taking cognizance filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 29299 of 2010 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before this Division for quashing the proceedings of the Special Case (then numbered as Metropolitan Special Case No: 132 of 2010) and after hearing the parties, their Lordships were pleased to issue Rule on 28- 9-2010 and stayed all further proceedings of Metropolitan Special Case No. 132 of 2010 pending before Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka, for a period of 6(six) months. On 7-4-2011 it was further extended till disposal of the Rule. Thereafter, a Division Bench of this court by their judgment and order dated 27-5-2013 discharged the Rule and vacated the order of stay and directed the trial Court to conclude trial as expeditiously as possible, challenging the judgment and order dated 27-5-2013 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous. Case No. 29299 of 2010, the accused-petitioner preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 241 of 2013 before the Hon'ble Appellate. Division; subsequently, the accused-petitioner filed a regular Criminal Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 369 of 2003 and the same is now pending for disposal before the Appellate Division, as such this application liable to be dismissed. He also submits that earlier opposite party No.2, the ACC preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.331 of 2010 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division against the ad-interim order dated 27-4-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Rule No. 235(FM) of 2010 arising out of FMA No. 218 of 20 1 0 and the Hon'ble Judge-in-Chamber of the Appellate Division stayed the same on 5-5-2010 for a period of 10 (ten) days with a direction to file regular leave petition, failing which the order of stay stand vacated; accordingly, opposite party No. 2 ACC filed regular Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 986 of2010 and the same was disposed of by the full court of the Hon'ble Appellate Division on 21-8-2011. 

 10. Learned advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission submits that the Hon'ble Appellate Division after hearing both the parties did not pass any order both in the Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No.241 of 2013 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 986 of 2010; the Hon'ble Appellate Division did not find any reason to stay the proceeding of the instant case. He further submits that the case of 14 BLC is not applicable in the instant case as there is a direction from' this Hon'ble Court to conclude trial of the instant case as expeditiously as possible; the Hon'ble Appellate Division after considering the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal did not pass any order to stay the instant proceeding; as such, there is no legal bar in continuation of this proceeding against the petitioner. He next submits that all other arguments as advance by the learned advocate for the petitioner are decided in the judgment and order dated 27-5-2013 passed by this Division, in the case of Mahmudur Rahman, vs The State, reported in 65 DLR 437; so, there is no legal bar in continuation of the proceeding by the trial court; there is no illegalities and irregularities in the impugned order of framing charge against this petitioner, as such, he prayed to reject the application summarily. 

 11. To substantiate his submission, learned advocate for the ACC placed reliance in the cases of Bangladesh vs Mosharraf Hossain, reported in 64 DLR (AD) 21, Mahmudur Rahman vs The State, reported in 65 DLR 437 and. The ACC vs Sheikh Hasina Wajed, reported in 60 DLR (AD 217. 

 "It is settled that when any matter in any manner appears or is reported to be pending before the Higher Forum, the subordinate courts can in no way proceed with any pending case before the same if said matter relates to the pending case. Even though the Hon'ble Appellate Division issued no stay order in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal being No.302/2006 filed by one accused of SC4942006 still then learned Sessions Judge was justified in staying further proceeding vide order dated 24-5-2007, subsequently learned Sessions Judge very rightly rejected the prayer of informant to vacate said earlier stay order opposing the prayer of the petition for issuing or Rule. 

 14. It is apparent from the FIR, charge-sheet and other materials on record that the ACC issued a notice on 13-4-2010 under section 26(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act-2004 directing the accused petitioner to submit his wealth statement within 7(seven) working days from the date of receipt of the notice. The informant stated that they sent the notice on 13-4-2010 to the accused- petitioner. However, after reading the said notice, the petitioner refused to accept the same. Subsequently, the notice was sent to him by registered post with AD. In the meantime, the petitioner filed a Civil Suit being Title Suit No. 250 of 2010 before the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, challenging legality of the proceeding initiated by the ACC pursuant to the said notice and in the plaint of the said Suit, he admitted that the said notice was received by him on 19-4-2010. The petitioner also filed an application for temporary injunction praying for stay of the proceedings initiated pursuant to the said notice and the learned Joint District Judge after hearing the parties rejected the same. Challenging the said judgment and order, the petitioner preferred appeal before this Hon'ble Court being FMA No. 218 of 2010 and after hearing the parties, their Lordships were pleased to issue Rule and stayed operation of the said notice and restrained the ACC to proceed any further pursuant to the said notice. Having aggrieved by the said order, the ACC preferred Civil Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No.331 of 2010 (Later converted into Civil Petition For leave to Appeal No. 968 of 2010) and after hearing the parties, the Hon'ble Judge-in- Chamber of the Appellate Division stayed operation of the said ad-interim order passed by the High Court Division vide order dated 5-5-2010. The petitioner failed to comply with the direction to submit wealth statement in time, as such, ACC filed the instant case against the petitioner under section 26(2)(Ka) of the said Act. 

 15. The accused petitioner after taking cognizance in the instant case filed Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 29299 of 2010 in this court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the instant proceedings and obtained Rule and an order of stay. Thereafter, a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court vide judgment and order dated 27-5-2013 discharged the Rule and vacated the order of stay directing the court below to conclude trial of the case as expeditiously as possible. 

 16. Challenging the said order, the accused petitioner preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 241 of 2013 (Later converted into Criminal Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 369 of 2013) and the same is now pending for hearing before the Appellate Division. 

 18. The Hon'ble Appellate Division after hearing both the parties did not pass any order of stay relating to the proceedings in both the Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 241 of 2013 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 986 of 2010. 

 19. In the case of Bangladesh vs Mosharraf Hossain, reported in 64 DLR (AD) 34, our apex Court held:- 

 20. In view of the above findings of our Apex Court, the decision reported in 14 BLC is not applicable in the instant case as there is no order of stay relating to impugned proceedings by the Hon'ble Appellate Division. Moreover, this Division vide judgment and order dated 27-5- 2013 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 29299 of 2010 directed the court below to conclude trial of the instant case as expeditiously as possible. As such, there is no legal bar in continuation of the instant proceeding against this petitioner rather it is obligatory upon the trial court to implement the judgment and order dated 27-5- 2013 according to the provisions of Article 111 of the Constitution. 

 22. We also find that the accused-petitioner filed Title Suit No. 250 of2010 before the learned Joint District Judge, 151 Court, Dhaka. In paragraph Nos. 24 and 27 of the plaint, the accused- petitioner made statement that the defendant No. 2 (Deputy Dircctor-2) (Training) issued notice bearing No. 4251 dated 10-3-2010 to the plaintiff, i.e. petitioner of this case, directing him to provide information relating to the following allegations:- 

 23. The plaintiff-petitioner was directed to be present in person before the Defendant No.2, ACC, on 16-3-2010 at 11-00 AM for the purpose of investigation. The ACC also sent another letter vide memo No. 2943 dated 17-2-2010 to the Securities and Exchange Commission to provide information relating to all shares, stocks and debentures of the plaintiff (petitioner) and his wife. After conducting necessary enquires, ACC issued notice on 13-4-2010, under section 26(1) of the Anti-corruption Act, 2004 directing the petitioner to submit his wealth statement within 07 (Seven) working days from the date of receipt of the said notice. The arguments as advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the ACC did not held enquiry into the matter before sending notice according to the provisions of section 26( 1) of the Anti -Corruption Act, bears no merit. From the petitioner's own admission in the plaint, it is evident that the ACC conducted an enquiry and provided ample opportunity to the petitioner to explain his position before it and sent the notice under section 26(1) of the ACC Act. Last Point raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner relating to the validity, legality and efficacy of the notice under section 26(1) of the said Act has been answered by this Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 29299 of 2010. 

 24. We have perused the FIR, Charge-sheet, impugned order and other relevant papers and documents annexed with the application, which disclose prima-facie case against the accused- petitioner. We do not find any illegality or irregularity in the impugned order dated 28-4-2014. 

 25. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and the principles enunciated by our Apex Court in the case of Bangladesh vs Mosarraf Hossain, reported in 64 DLR (AD) 34, we find nothing to interfere with the impugned order dated 28-4-2014 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka, in Special case No. 17 of2010.
